summary.en-US: Select a passage or type an idea, and every sentence on the page is colored by how close it is in meaning. By default, all data is processed locally in your browser.

description.en-US:
Select a sentence or a passage, or type an idea into the search box, and the rest of the page lights up as a heatmap: related ideas turn yellow, orange and red, unrelated ones stay faint blue. You can see where an article comes back to the same idea even when it uses different words.

How to use it:
• Press Ctrl+Shift+F (Control+Shift+F on a Mac) or click the toolbar button on a page.
• Type an idea and press Enter, or select text. Related sentences are colored at once.
• The strip on the right edge marks where the matches are; click a mark to jump. ▲ ▼ step through them, best match first.
• Esc clears the colors; the button, ✕, or Ctrl+Shift+F pressed in the search box turn it off.
• Or right-click a selection → "Highlight sentences related to…".

Private: a small embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 23 MB) runs inside the browser. It is downloaded once from Hugging Face; by default, all data is processed locally and the extension sends none of it anywhere. A multilingual model (118 MB, matches Hebrew to English and 50+ other languages) and a local Ollama server are options.

Leaves the page alone: colors are painted with the CSS Custom Highlight API, so the page itself is never modified.

Runs only where you turn it on: nothing is injected until you press the shortcut or click the button on a tab.

Open source (MIT): https://github.com/NimbleShot/semantic-highlighter

release_notes.en-US:
• Search box: type an idea and press Enter to color the page by it, as well as selecting text. A selection's text appears in the box so it can be edited.
• New shortcut Ctrl+Shift+F (Control+Shift+F on a Mac): opens the search box, and pressed again in the box turns the highlighter off. The old Alt+Shift+H shortcut is gone: Alt opened Firefox's menu bar. The toolbar button still turns it on and off.
• Shortcut hints in the tooltips and the options page show the keys actually set.

version.approval_notes:
Build from the attached source: Node 20+, then `npm ci && npm run build`; the add-on is dist/firefox. The bundle is made by esbuild from src/ plus @huggingface/transformers 4.3.0 from npm. (dist/firefox-test is a test-only build and is not the submitted add-on.)

Changes since 0.1.0: a search box in the on-page pill, and the shortcut moved from Alt+Shift+H to Ctrl+Shift+F (a new command, search-by-meaning). No new permissions.

The linter's UNSAFE_VAR_ASSIGNMENT warning on a dynamic import() in background.js is inside onnxruntime-web (bundled by transformers.js). The URL it imports is set in src/engine.js to the packaged file ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.mjs via runtime.getURL; no remote code is loaded.

Network: the background page downloads the model weights (ONNX + tokenizer JSON, data only) from huggingface.co on first use. If the user picks Ollama in the options, sentences are sent to the server URL they enter, after an optional host permission prompt.

To test: open any article (e.g. a Wikipedia page), press Ctrl+Shift+F, wait for the pill to finish reading the page, then type an idea and press Enter, or select a sentence.
